subtopics.title: Charge, the Coulomb, and the Statement of the Law

questions.question: Coulomb's law states that the force between two point charges is:
options: Proportional to the product of the charge magnitudes and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them
Proportional to the sum of the charges and inversely proportional to the distance
Inversely proportional to the product of the charges

questions.question: A sphere carries −4,8 × 10⁻⁶ C. The number of excess electrons on it is:
Charges of +3 μC and −5 μC are held 0,15 m apart. The force between them is:
The signs of the charges are kept OUT of the substitution because:
options: The constant k already carries the signs
The signs are irrelevant to electrostatics
They only answer a separate question — whether the force attracts or repels — which is stated in words

subtopics.title: Three Charges in a Straight Line

questions.question: When finding the net force on one charge among several, each neighbouring charge is handled:
options: In one separate Coulomb calculation, as if the other neighbours did not exist
By adding all the charges first
By using the average of all the distances

questions.question: A (+3 μC), B (−2 μC) and C (+4 μC) lie in a line with B between them. The force of A on B points:
options: Away from A, since B is negative
Toward A, because unlike charges attract

questions.question: With 1,35 N pulling B left and 0,8 N pulling B right, the net force on B is:
B sits 0,2 m from A and 0,3 m from C. The distance 0,5 m (A to C) is used:
options: Nowhere — each pair keeps its own separation, and A-to-C is not a pair involving B

subtopics.title: Charges at Right Angles — Coulomb's Law in Two Dimensions

questions.question: Q1 (+2 μC) has Q2 (−5 μC) 0,5 m to its north and Q3 (+3 μC) 0,3 m to its east. The two forces on Q1 point:
options: North (attraction to Q2) and west (repulsion from Q3)

questions.question: The magnitudes are 0,36 N and 0,6 N at right angles. The resultant is:
The direction of that resultant is:
The correct order of operations for right-angle charge problems is:
options: Pythagoras first, then find the two forces
Sketch and reason each direction, calculate each magnitude, then Pythagoras and inverse tangent
Add the three charges, then divide by the distances
Calculate both magnitudes, then guess the quadrant

subtopics.title: Touching Spheres and the Exam Traps

questions.question: Identical spheres carrying +8 μC and −4 μC touch and separate. Each sphere afterwards carries:
options: +2 μC, the signed total shared equally

questions.question: Before touching, the force between them (0,2 m apart) was 7,2 N attractive. After touching it becomes:
The r in Coulomb's law for two charged spheres is measured between their:
Halving the distance between two fixed charges changes the force to:
When a jersey is rubbed over your hair, charging happens because:
options: Electrons are scraped from one surface onto the other — charge moves, none is created
Protons jump from hair to jersey
New charge is created by the friction

questions.question: Freshly rubbed hair strands lift away from EACH OTHER because:
options: They are attracted to the ceiling
Each strand carries the same sign of charge, and likes repel
They have lost all their charge

questions.question: Real charged objects carry microcoulombs rather than whole coulombs because:
options: The coulomb is defined only for metals
Electrons are too heavy to accumulate
A whole coulomb is an enormous charge — even a millionth of one contains around ten million million electrons
Charge cannot exist above a microcoulomb

questions.question: Coulomb's law and Newton's law of gravitation share the same skeleton:
options: Multiply the two sources, divide by the distance squared
Add the two sources, divide by the distance
Multiply the sources and the distance
Divide the sources by each other

questions.question: Doubling both charges while doubling the distance leaves the force:
options: Unchanged — times four from the charges, divided by four from the distance

questions.question: A key DIFFERENCE between the two laws is:
options: Coulomb's law only works in vacuum
Gravity is stronger between everyday objects
Gravity only attracts, while the electric force can attract or repel

questions.question: A rubbed balloon lifts a scrap of paper against the whole Earth's gravity because:
options: The electric constant is enormous, so small charges out-pull planetary gravity at close range
The Earth's gravity switches off near balloons

subtopics.title: The Tug-of-War on the Middle Charge

questions.question: The first step in any middle-charge problem is to:
options: Draw one arrow per neighbour, from attraction or repulsion, before any calculation

questions.question: The two arrows on the middle charge point in the SAME direction. You should:
options: Subtract the smaller from the larger

questions.question: Each neighbour's force on the middle charge is computed using:
options: The total distance across all three charges
That neighbour's own distance to the middle charge
The average of the two distances
The distance between the two outer charges

questions.question: If one neighbour is north and the other east, the combined force on the corner charge comes from:
options: Pythagoras on the two perpendicular arrows — e.g. 0,36 and 0,6 give 0,7
